items: A round-topped window: h is the height to the springing, arch is the rise above it. The hole in the wall stays rectangular.
A bullseye, centred at sill + r. w and h are the square hole the frame covers — keep them at 2r.
A three-sided glazed box projecting out of the wall by depth.
A ribbon window: one long light divided by slim mullions.
Two sliding glass leaves — a patio or terrace door.
Two glazed timber leaves opening onto a garden.
A glazed facade panel: a mullion/transom grid filled with glass. It REPLACES a wall face, it is not an opening.
